tutorial.title: Comparing Strings
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to check if two strings are the same.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: We can use comparisons to check if a string is equal to or not equal to another string.

lessons.title: Equality operator
lessons.interactiveContent:
To check if a string is equal to another string, we can use the strict equality operator, ===.

Make sure to pick ===.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To check if a string is equal to another string, we can use the strict equality operator, ===.

Use === to compare matching strings and display true.

Make sure to pick "apple", followed by ===, and finally "apple".

lessons.title: True
lessons.interactiveContent:
If the string on the left is equal to the string on the right, as in "apple" === "apple", the result is true.

Make sure to pick "apple", followed by ===, and finally "apple".
lessons.hardModeContent:
If the string on the left equals the string on the right, as in "apple" === "apple", the result is true.

Compare first with second for equality, keeping first on the left.

Make sure to pick first, followed by ===, and finally second.

lessons.title: False
lessons.interactiveContent:
If the string on the left isn't equal to the string on the right, as in "apple" === "orange", the result is false.

Make sure to pick ===, followed by "orange".
lessons.hardModeContent:
If the string on the left is not equal to the string on the right, the equality comparison gives false.

Compare "apple" with "orange" for equality, keeping "apple" on the left.

Make sure to pick "apple", followed by ===, and finally "orange".

lessons.title: Comparing the same string
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also compare variables that store strings with each other, like in fruit1 === fruit2.

Make sure to pick fruit1, followed by ===, and finally fruit2.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can also compare variables that store strings with each other.

Compare fruit1 with fruit2 for equality, keeping fruit1 on the left.

Make sure to pick fruit1, followed by ===, and finally fruit2.

lessons.title: Using the not equal operator
lessons.interactiveContent:
To check if a string isn't equal to another string, we use the strict inequality operator, !==.

Make sure to pick !==.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To check if a string isn't equal to another string, we use the strict inequality operator, !==.

Use !== to make the comparison display true.

Make sure to pick !==, followed by "orange".

lessons.title: True
lessons.interactiveContent:
If the string on the left isn't equal to the string on the right, as in "apple" !== "orange", the result is true.

Make sure to pick !==, followed by "orange".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Different strings, such as "apple" and "orange", make !== return true.

Check whether first is not equal to second, keeping first on the left.

Make sure to pick first, followed by !==, and finally second.

lessons.title: False
lessons.interactiveContent: If the string on the left is equal to the string on the right, as in "orange" !== "orange", the result is false.
